title: Stone Shelter Product Specification

sections.title: 1 Product purpose and release boundary
sections.sources: Original README, constitution, glossary, features 0001 through 0029 and the four supplied screenshots
sections.intro:
Stone Shelter is an English-language educational application in which visitors discover collectible stones, read their stories and care guidance, and submit an adoption request. Volunteers maintain the catalog and complete the adoption process. A grounded assistant helps visitors choose a suitable available stone and understand its care. The first release is a complete local, single-backend application with real persistent catalog data and explicitly separate developer mock mode.

This is the implementation baseline for a new checkout. It consolidates the source project as of 24 October 2026 and makes product decisions under the user's explicit delegation. It is not a claim that the source application satisfies the requirements. All newly selected behavior is identified in the decision register. Historical task approvals, exclusions and test results are evidence about earlier work, not instructions to execute or guarantees about this release.

requirements.title: Release outcome
requirements.text: Deliver browsing, details, protected catalog management, image handling, adoption request and volunteer resolution, grounded chat, indexing recovery and the delivery gates in this document. Ship these as staged increments W01–W08; the complete release requires all increments. No payment, shipping, legal transfer of ownership, medical benefit or automated contact promise is made by an adoption request.

requirements.title: Authority and change control
requirements.text: This baseline defines target behavior; the decision register explains deviations from historical sources. Screenshots establish visual direction and visible workflows, not hidden rules or success evidence. Requirements and scenarios are authored once in specification.json and rendered into this Word document. A later behavior change updates that source, affected decisions and scenarios before code changes. Generated OpenAPI and maintained AsyncAPI implement the contract requirements; this document is not a second handwritten OpenAPI schema.

requirements.title: Actors and privileges
requirements.text: Visitor: read public catalog/details, use anonymous owned chat and submit an adoption request. Volunteer: authenticate, manage all catalog records and photos, review contact details and resolve applications. Operator: all volunteer permissions plus document indexing, reindexing, diagnostics and staff provisioning. Deny other actions by default and check permission and object ownership on each server operation. A hidden button is not authorization. No public registration or user account is required to browse or apply. [E03]

requirements.title: Deliberate scope boundary
requirements.text: This release supports English, one shelter, one active backend and local Ollama. Preserve a provider interface but do not ship external-provider fallback, multi-instance execution, payment, delivery scheduling, email/SMS automation, favorites, social accounts or a ticket-board integration. Search analytics remains a later product increment; operational counters without raw messages are required now. These are explicit baseline exclusions, not unresolved decisions.

sections.title: 2 Domain rules and data ownership
sections.intro: A stone is an individual specimen. Type-level encyclopedia knowledge describes a category and cannot establish an unrecorded property of that specimen. A reservation represents an adoption application; RESERVED is not ADOPTED. Database constraints enforce lifecycle invariants as well as application validation.

requirements.title: Stone vocabulary
requirements.text: Supported stoneType values, in filter order, are BASALT, GRANITE, OBSIDIAN, PUMICE, LIMESTONE, SANDSTONE, SHALE, MARBLE, GNEISS and SLATE. stoneSize is SMALL, MEDIUM or LARGE, with that domain sort order. adoptionStatus is AVAILABLE, RESERVED or ADOPTED. API enums are case-sensitive; UI labels are title case. IDs are positive integers no greater than 9007199254740991 and are never reused. A separate immutable UUID identifies storage objects.

requirements.title: Stone field constraints
requirements.text: name is required, trimmed, 1–120 Unicode code points; duplicate names are allowed. stoneType and stoneSize are required. biography is optional plain text, at most 2048 code points; preserve its internal whitespace and line breaks, map an all-whitespace value to null. Reject control characters other than tab/newline in biography and contact text; name has no line breaks. Count Unicode code points consistently in browser and server. No user field is interpreted as HTML.

requirements.title: Authoritative dates and status
requirements.text: Creation sets admissionDate once from the server UTC clock and adoptionStatus to AVAILABLE. Clients cannot assign either; reject these write properties with 400. Dates are UTC instants serialized with Z and displayed as UTC calendar dates. Ordinary editing cannot change admissionDate or adoptionStatus. Reservation transitions own status changes. Existing historical instants remain unchanged when a migration imports data; migration is a separately executed, explicitly scoped operation.

requirements.title: Versions and deletion
requirements.text: Maintain a row version for lost-update protection and a distinct monotonically increasing indexing sourceVersion. Updates and deletions of existing stones or reservations require the current ETag via If-Match; missing precondition is 428 and stale is 412. Deleting a stone with an active application returns 409 until it is resolved. Authorized deletion removes public visibility and metadata transactionally, closes no application implicitly, emits an index tombstone and queues photo cleanup; retain a minimal ID/version tombstone so stale events cannot resurrect it.

requirements.title: Field ownership and privacy
requirements.text: Public responses expose stone ID, name, type, size, biography, status, admissionDate and ordered public photo representations only. Applicant identity/contact, staff credentials, storage keys, model prompts, index scores and audit details are never public stone fields. Private application history is accessible only to authorized staff. Preserve historical chat responses as originally committed; clicking an old reference rechecks the current detail route.

sections.title: 3 Catalog navigation and filtering
sections.intro: The catalog is the starting point. It combines a collapsible filter sidebar, active-filter chips, result count, sort control, responsive cards and pagination. The Add stone action is available to authenticated staff; visitors see a discreet Staff sign in link in the footer.

requirements.title: Canonical navigation
requirements.text: Use /stone-shelter/catalog, /stone-shelter/stones/{id} and /stone-shelter/add-stone. Redirect /, /stone-shelter, /stones/new and /stones/{id} to their canonical equivalents with history replacement; normalize one trailing slash. Serve SPA fallback on direct entry/refresh. The shared brand links to the catalog. Unknown routes show Page not found; malformed or missing stone IDs show Stone not found. Preserve native modified-click/new-tab behavior.

requirements.title: Visibility and result integrity
requirements.text: Public search returns only AVAILABLE stones. Apply this invariant before filters, ordering, total count and pagination. Direct detail reads may show RESERVED and ADOPTED stones with an unavailable action. A requested non-AVAILABLE status cannot widen public visibility. Count is total matching records, not the current card count; zero matches is a successful empty state, separate from an error.

requirements.title: Filter semantics
requirements.text: Support multi-select sizes and types and an optional admission-date range. OR values within each group; AND groups. A From date includes its UTC midnight, a To date includes the whole UTC day through exclusive next-day midnight. Allow open bounds and future search bounds. Reject impossible dates or From after To. Invalid drafts keep the last valid applied range and page, show a field error and allow valid type/size changes independently. Empty arrays mean no restriction; deduplicate values and reject unknown/null array members.

requirements.title: Multiselect and chips
requirements.text: Size and Stone type dropdowns use a search field and native checkboxes. Match trimmed option queries case-insensitively against labels without changing catalog filters or order. Show “No matching options.” when empty. Selecting applies immediately and retains the query; closing clears only that query. Each trigger counts selected values, including zero. The sidebar badge counts active groups, 0–3. Chips list sizes then types in option order, then one date-range chip; removing one chip changes only its value or the date group. Chips remain usable during loading, error and empty results.

requirements.title: Sort and pagination
requirements.text: Offer Newest first, Oldest first, Name A–Z, Name Z–A, Size small–large and Size large–small. Map these to admissionDate/name/stoneSize with ASC or DESC and ID ASC as a stable tie-breaker. Default Newest first. UI page size defaults to 8 with choices 8, 12 and 24; backend default remains 12, maximum 24. API page is zero-based; UI page is one-based. Filter/sort/page-size changes reset to page 1. An out-of-range API page returns an empty page; UI refresh after a removal loads the last valid page once.

requirements.title: Reset and navigational state
requirements.text: Reset filters clears selected sizes/types, applied/draft dates, errors and option search text, returns to page 1 and preserves sort, page size and sidebar expansion. Keep applied catalog state and scroll in application memory across details, Back/Forward and Back to catalog; direct entry and full reload use defaults. Do not encode transient controls or contact information in URLs. URL-persisted filters are deliberately outside this release.

requirements.title: Catalog presentation and request races
requirements.text: Cards show cover or shared placeholder, name, type, size and a two-line biography excerpt; the detail page shows full text. A photo/name link names its destination accessibly. Show a result count, distinct loading, retryable error and empty states. Ignore obsolete responses after a newer search. Retain current filter controls during fetches. Grid has 4 columns at viewport width at least 960 CSS px, 2 at 560–959 and 1 below 560, reducing within the available content area if side panels would violate usable card width.

requirements.title: Filter panel interaction
requirements.text: At first mount the sidebar is open at widths at least 960 CSS px and closed below that. Desktop collapse reclaims space. On smaller widths the panel is modal: labelled dialog, focus within, inert background, scroll lock, close/backdrop/Escape dismissal and focus restoration. Resize preserves the chosen state while switching semantics. Escape first closes the innermost dropdown, then the panel on a later keypress. Chip removal focuses the next chip, previous chip or catalog heading, in that order. [E02]

sections.title: 4 Stone details and image lifecycle
sections.intro: Details pair a prominent gallery with the specimen name, ID, availability, adoption action, characteristics and biography. Photo operations use private object storage and durable metadata; database success and transfer progress are represented separately.

requirements.title: Detail states and gallery
requirements.text: Show full biography with line breaks, or This stone’s story is coming soon. Display UTC admission date and all characteristics. Gallery order determines the cover; local thumbnail selection never changes it. Zero images show one shared English placeholder and no fabricated thumbnails. One image needs no strip arrows. Multiple images use a bounded keyboard/touch-accessible strip, labelled selected thumbnail and main-image alternative text. Broken images fall back once without a request loop. Reserve image dimensions to avoid layout shifts.

requirements.title: Upload bounds and content validation
requirements.text: Allow 0–16 photos per stone across every creation and append path. A photo is a nonempty JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 10 MiB (10485760 bytes); decoded dimensions may not exceed 25 million pixels. Check extension, declared type, signature and successful bounded decoding; do not trust Content-Type alone. Reject animated content and SVG. Strip metadata such as EXIF location and re-encode an accepted image before storage. Generate storage names server-side, preserve orientation and never use client path names. Only staff may upload. [E04]

requirements.title: Drafts and creation atomicity
requirements.text: Upload drafts separately before creation; associate each draft with the authenticated staff identity. A draft expires exactly 24 hours after successful upload, has a UUID and can be claimed once. Creation accepts ordered distinct photoUploadIds, at most 16. In one transaction validate ownership, lifetime and unclaimed state, create the stone, claim every draft, assign positions and save its index outbox event. A failed transaction creates none of these; valid drafts remain reusable until expiry. A foreign draft behaves as not found. Concurrent claims have one winner; other attempts return 409.

requirements.title: Durable photo transfer
requirements.text: After commit, a durable worker copies claimed draft content into permanent storage. Public photo entries expose processingStatus PENDING, READY or FAILED; only READY exposes an expiring image URL, others show the placeholder. A failed copy does not erase the stone or report creation failure. Retry transient failures after 1, 5, 30, 120 and 360 minutes after the preceding failure; after the sixth failed total attempt mark FAILED and expose a staff Retry transfer action. Keep the claimed source until READY or explicit removal; never silently expire the sole copy.

requirements.title: Photo ownership and updates
requirements.text: Staff may append, remove, reorder and choose cover by moving an image to position zero. Apply the 16-photo cap and unique positions under a stone row lock, with If-Match. Reorder submits all current photo IDs exactly once; unknown, omitted or duplicate IDs are 400. Removing a pending/failed photo releases its source to cleanup. Staff retries require a retained source, otherwise 409 with Replace photo guidance. A visitor cannot mutate gallery state. The add form can reorder drafts before creation with keyboard Move earlier/later controls.

requirements.title: Private storage and URL expiry
requirements.text: Store bucket/key and lifecycle metadata, never a signed URL, as durable truth. Photo buckets are private. READY URLs live for at most one hour; draft preview URLs for at most one hour and no longer than draft lifetime. Refresh a failed expired display URL at most once through the authorized read API before showing a recoverable error. No public draft enumeration or original filename disclosure. New writes do not accept the old arbitrary photo URL field; imported external URLs must be converted by an explicitly authorized migration or use the placeholder.

requirements.title: Deferred cleanup and operational recovery
requirements.text: Request handlers never delete object bytes inline. Persist cleanup intentions with metadata changes, including rollback compensation and removed drafts. Unclaimed drafts become eligible after 24 hours; run bounded cleanup hourly with a maximum of 100 objects or 60 seconds per pass. Check readiness and ownership before each removal, protect attached sources with a database lock, and retain failed intents across restart. Stop a pass on storage failure, log a nonsecret cause and retry on the next pass. Record queue age and failed-transfer counts; alert locally when the oldest due item exceeds 24 hours.

sections.title: 5 Creating and maintaining stones
sections.sources: Screenshot 4 and features 0003, 0008, 0009, 0011; access control and recovery are baseline additions
sections.intro: The form keeps the screenshot's fields and optional-photo workflow while replacing sixteen empty boxes with useful previews and an Add photos control. Submission success means the stone and its durable work were saved; it does not imply that every background transfer or embedding is complete.

requirements.title: Create form interaction
requirements.text: Require Name, Stone type and Size, initially empty. Biography and photos are optional; no admission-date, adoption-status or URL input appears. Show photo count /16, supported formats and 10 MiB limit next to the picker. Display only selected previews plus an Add photos control; use responsive tiles rather than sixteen empty placeholders. Keep selection order, first-image cover and remove/reorder controls. Zero photos submits an empty array and uploads no placeholder file.

requirements.title: Upload batches and error preservation
requirements.text: Validate a newly selected file batch before sending it, retaining previous selections if rejected. Upload valid files with bounded concurrency of two and preserve selection order despite completion order. Retain successful drafts on a mixed failure and identify each failed file. While a batch settles, form fields remain editable but Create and gallery mutation controls are disabled. On create failure retain field values and valid drafts; refresh/reupload only expired or failed entries, never all successful photos automatically.

requirements.title: Submit and confirmation
requirements.text: Validate fields, focus the first error and prevent duplicate submission while pending. Use one UUID Idempotency-Key per intentional create; a transport retry reuses its exact payload/key. After confirmed creation show “Stone added successfully.”, name, ID, cover or transfer status, View stone, Back to catalog and Add another. Keep this on the creation route until navigation; Add another starts a clean form. Unsaved navigation offers Keep editing or Discard; pending navigation warns that saving may still finish and offers Stay or Leave, without issuing another write.

requirements.title: Staff editing and deletion
requirements.text: Staff detail controls lead to /stone-shelter/stones/{id}/edit for name, type, size, biography and gallery management, using the same validation and preview components. Save requires If-Match; stale data prompts reload and preserves the unsaved draft for comparison without overwriting silently. Delete requires a confirmation naming the stone; success returns to the catalog and refreshes it. An active reservation blocks deletion. Status transitions occur only through the reservation workflow, never a free-form dropdown.

requirements.title: Write replay semantics
requirements.text: For stone creation and reservation submission, bind Idempotency-Key to actor or anonymous application session, route, target and canonical payload hash. Save successful response/status with the business transaction for 72 hours. Same identity/payload replays the original outcome; changed payload is 409. Keep a minimal used-key hash marker for 90 days and return 409 after response expiry instead of recreating work. Validation rejection before execution does not consume a key. An active or uncertain attempt is reconciled, never assumed rolled back because its HTTP response was lost. Store a server-keyed payload digest for comparison; do not retain raw applicant contact data in an idempotency record after its private-data retention expires.

sections.title: 6 Adoption applications and volunteer completion
sections.sources: Screenshot 3 and feature 0007; the complete lifecycle is a new product decision
sections.intro: A successful visitor application places one temporary hold on the stone. A volunteer contacts the applicant outside the application, records the outcome and completes or releases the hold. This closes the gap between the screenshot's Submit application action and a usable adoption process.

requirements.title: Application modal
requirements.text: Adopt this stone is enabled only for AVAILABLE details. The labelled modal shows the cover, name and ID, Your name, Contact details and Submit application. Name is required, trimmed, 1–120 code points; Contact details is required, trimmed, 1–1000, accepts plain-text contact preferences without an email-only regex. Explain that details are used to arrange the adoption and removed according to the stated retention. Focus the name initially; trap focus, make the background inert and restore focus on close. Closing preserves the draft for that stone during the page session; another stone starts empty. [E02]

requirements.title: Atomic hold and concurrency
requirements.text: In one database transaction lock the stone by ID, expire any already-due hold, verify effective AVAILABLE status, create one PENDING application, set RESERVED and save the idempotent result. Enforce at most one active PENDING application per stone with a database constraint. Return 201 only after commit. Other simultaneous applicants receive 409 and no application. Missing stone is 404; invalid input is 400. A completed or cancelled historical application does not prevent a future active application after the stone has legitimately become AVAILABLE.

requirements.title: Visitor outcome and recovery
requirements.text: On success keep the modal open with “Application submitted. Please wait for us to contact you.”, an application reference and its UTC hold expiry. Refresh details to RESERVED and remove the stone from the public catalog while preserving catalog choices. A refresh failure cannot erase submission success; show a separate refresh action. On 409 preserve entered text, explain no longer available and refresh status. On an ambiguous network result keep the same key and offer explicit retry, not a second application. Do not show ADOPTED after mere submission.

requirements.title: Reservation state machine
requirements.text: PENDING holds last 72 hours from creation. Before expiresAt, an authorized volunteer may COMPLETE, CANCEL or REJECT with an optional 500-character note; COMPLETE changes application to COMPLETED and stone to ADOPTED, CANCEL/REJECT change it to CANCELLED/REJECTED and stone to AVAILABLE. At or after expiresAt only EXPIRE is valid, changing it to EXPIRED and stone to AVAILABLE. Resolve transitions under the same stone/application lock; a second incompatible transition returns 409. Terminal records do not reopen. Staff may extend a PENDING hold once by 72 hours before expiry, with a required reason.

requirements.title: Expiry and staff work queue
requirements.text: Run expiry every minute; public reads/search and mutation guards also account for logically expired holds so scheduler delay cannot make a stone unavailable indefinitely. Do not report an expired hold as still adoptable only to reject the next application. Staff queue /stone-shelter/staff/applications lists PENDING by earliest expiry and terminal items by latest update, with status filter, pagination size 20 and a detail panel showing contacts and actions. Completion records the acting staff ID and time; contact is manual, not an automated email promise.

requirements.title: Application retention and abuse control
requirements.text: Purge applicant name, contact and private notes 30 days after terminal status, preserving anonymous application ID, stone ID, status/timestamps and staff action audit for 90 days. Restrict reads, avoid logging PII and use synthetic test contacts. Apply a shared atomic application limit of 3 submissions per 10 minutes per anonymous session and 20 per hour per IP, returning 429 with Retry-After. Cookie loss does not bypass the IP gate. Reject unavailable protection storage with 503 before mutating. Expiry and retention are chosen product policies, not claims of legal compliance.

sections.title: 7 Chat conversation and streaming
sections.intro: The assistant is available on catalog and detail pages and is clearly separate from staff operations. It helps with discovery and care; it never submits an application, changes a stone or asks for contact information. API mode uses real backend state and never silently switches to a demo.

requirements.title: Widget and composer
requirements.text: Start collapsed with a round green launcher. Expanded panel is named Stone Shelter Chat, with a local greeting, four initial quick prompts: Help me choose a stone; Tell me about stone properties; How do I care for a stone?; Another topic, scrollable history and a labelled composer. Input is nonblank, at most 2000 Unicode code points, sent literally; Enter sends except during IME composition, Shift+Enter inserts a newline. Hide initial prompts after the first submission. One visible user message and one assistant message represent each turn. Keep typed draft editable while pending but disable further sends/retries/prompts.

requirements.title: Session ownership and retention
requirements.text: Use a server-issued opaque anonymous HttpOnly, host-only, SameSite=Lax cookie, Secure over HTTPS, and a tab conversation UUID in sessionStorage. UUID and IP are not ownership credentials. Foreign retained conversation IDs return 404. Redis stores complete ordered user/assistant pairs, submitted context, returned references, turnId and saved replay result for 24 hours after the latest new committed pair. Reads, replay and navigation do not refresh server retention. A lost Redis transcript is recoverable as empty only after a successful authoritative read, never during an outage. Limit a conversation to 200 completed pairs; reject a new turn beyond that with 409 CHAT_CONVERSATION_FULL and offer Start new conversation. Preserve existing history within its TTL instead of silently discarding old pairs.

requirements.title: Turn identity and navigation
requirements.text: Generate turnId once per intentional send and capture literal message and page stoneId at that moment. Retry keeps all three unchanged; changed payload for a retained identity is 409. New identical text gets a new turnId. Keep active work, draft, open state and messages above page routing; collapse/navigation must not cancel or duplicate a send. Reload restores only server history, collapsed with empty draft, and never reconstructs or resends a pending request. History reconciliation merges by role and turnId.

requirements.title: Chat readiness separation
requirements.text: Fail new model work closed when identity, quota, history, serialization, catalog/evidence, provider or accounting prerequisites cannot be verified. Model outage alone must not prevent authorized healthy history reads, committed replay or conversation deletion; these require their own identity/storage/quota dependencies. Never replace unavailable history with an empty transcript. UI preserves displayed text and offers manual recovery. A recovery attempt validates required components and reconciles history before enabling new sends. Readiness has component-specific capability results, not one global green flag.

requirements.title: Rate and concurrency controls
requirements.text: Use atomic session and IP token buckets. Sends: session burst 3 with 10/min refill, IP burst 10 with 60/min refill. History: session burst 5 with 30/min refill, IP burst 20 with 120/min refill. Charge IP before anonymous session allocation, then session quota; do not refund consumed request tokens on later busy/error. Return 429 and a positive rounded-up Retry-After for exhaustion. Serialize one active turn per conversation, zero queue, through an owned 150-second renewable lease and a local permit retained until actual worker exit; renew every 30 seconds and fence commits. Busy conversation is 429 with Retry-After 1.

requirements.title: Stream lifecycle
requirements.text: POST /api/v1/chat/messages/stream uses the same pipeline as JSON. Named SSE events are started, text-delta, completed and error with conversationId, turnId and contiguous positive sequence starting at 1. Commit a validated complete answer/pair before emitting answer text. Concatenated nonempty deltas exactly equal completed.text; references appear only in completed. A retained replay uses started then completed with no new model work or TTL refresh. HTTP 200 and EOF alone never imply completion. [E06]

requirements.title: Disconnect and incomplete display
requirements.text: Disconnect stops delivery, not admitted processing; execution may finish within its original deadline. Before completed, retain received text visibly marked Incomplete, without links, and offer Check saved answer. Reconcile against authoritative history; an absent turn while work might run is not proof of rollback. Manual retry is allowed only with the original identity after successful recovery. Never auto-reconnect, auto-resend through JSON or replay speculative text. After completed, keep the confirmed answer even if later history synchronization fails, and do not offer resend of that completed turn.

requirements.title: Bounded transport and cookie timing
requirements.text: Limit four open streams per backend, including replay, with no queue; excess returns 503 CHAT_STREAM_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED and Retry-After 1 before model work. Use 15-second preparation heartbeat comments, at most one pending frame, 256-code-point chunks, 10-second delivery/write timeout and a 135-second browser read bound. Heartbeats extend no deadline. Newly admitted streams may synchronize the cookie before headers; only committed pairs extend server lifetimes. Healthy authorized history GET synchronizes cookie expiry to remaining server lifetime, never recreating ownership.

requirements.title: New conversation and data clearing
requirements.text: Provide Start new conversation with a confirmation if a draft exists, and Clear this conversation. A new conversation retains session quotas and changes only the tab UUID. Clear is an authorized DELETE for the current conversation; reject active turns with 409, then atomically delete transcript/owner/replay data and rotate the UI UUID. Explain that clearing removes retry recovery for old turns. Never clear another tab's conversation or reset quotas. The old tab binding receives an empty healthy read only after deletion is confirmed.

requirements.title: Accessible chat behavior
requirements.text: The chat is nonmodal, enters composer focus on open and returns focus to the launcher on explicit close/Escape. Other modal flows make chat inert. At desktop reserve chat space only when enough width remains; otherwise float the panel without obscuring focused controls. Fit 320 CSS px and keep header/composer visible. Follow new content only within 80 px of the bottom; otherwise preserve reading position and offer Jump to latest. Announce waiting, one completed reply and errors, not every delta. API labels omit Demo; developer mock mode is explicitly labelled.

sections.title: 8 Grounded search and answers
sections.intro: The backend validates an interpreted request and executes bounded operations. Models cannot execute arbitrary SQL, select public record IDs freely, invoke write tools or change authorization. Search quality and factual correctness are evaluated separately from transport success.

requirements.title: Intent and exact search
requirements.text: Interpret each new turn once with at most one repair call. Support exact type, size, availability and UTC date constraints, semantic wishes, knowledge questions, mixed requests and trusted references. OR values/ranges within a group and AND groups. Relative today/yesterday use the server UTC date; an explicit calendar day/month without a year requires clarification. An explicit request to show all available stones may return the newest five with the exact count and an invitation to refine; a vague I want a stone asks a focused question. Never silently drop a requested condition.

requirements.title: Follow up and reference rules
requirements.text: A follow-up replaces explicitly changed constraints and retains unchanged ones, including negation; Start a new search clears them. Knowledge-only questions do not reset selection state. Resolve ordinals from the last actual nonempty selection and this stone from captured page context. Ambiguous, deleted or unavailable references lead to clarification without substitution. Literal name/ID text is not a new general search filter; ask the visitor to open a catalog record or clarify. Do not treat a knowledge convenience link as a replacement selection list.

requirements.title: Exact results and empty outcomes
requirements.text: Exact results are AVAILABLE only, ordered admissionDate DESC then ID ASC. Compute the full filtered database count, present at most five current IDs/names and mention more results when applicable. If no exact results exist, state that clearly and optionally suggest a filter the visitor could relax; never relax it without a new intentional request. Knowledge-only questions can be answered without a catalog match. Pure exact searches require no semantic embedding or model-generated result wording.

requirements.title: Semantic evidence and candidate retrieval
requirements.text: Embed effective semantic wishes once and reuse the vector for card and document retrieval. Apply current existence, AVAILABLE and exact constraints before candidate limits. Initial candidate limit 10, document limit 10, inclusive cosine thresholds 0.5; invalid supplied configuration fails rather than defaulting silently. Candidate recall may come from factual card similarity or applicable type passages; absence of a card vector alone does not exclude a type-supported candidate. Similarity is a ranking signal, not proof. Check every wish as supported, unknown or contradicted against supplied current facts and cited source spans.

requirements.title: Evidence hierarchy and truthful ranking
requirements.text: Current individual facts outrank type-level knowledge. A card contradiction excludes a candidate, even from exact alternatives; general typical color cannot prove an individual stone's color. At least one wish must be supported for a semantic match; identify unmet wishes. Rank card-supported candidates first by card similarity, then type-only candidates by strongest applicable passage similarity, ID ASC for ties. Present at most five; count only the bounded checked pool and never claim an exhaustive semantic total. A nonempty semantic list is not filled with unverified alternatives.

requirements.title: Alternatives and concurrent changes
requirements.text: Only when no semantic candidates qualify and usable exact constraints exist may the backend offer bounded exact alternatives, explicitly labelled as not confirmed for the semantic wishes. Semantic-only requests never fall back to arbitrary AVAILABLE stones. Recheck the full pool against current facts, constraints and availability before commit. Remove invalid items and associated text, retaining a smaller surviving set. If a previously valid pool becomes entirely ineligible, allow one retrieval refresh for the whole turn with existing interpretation/vector/counters. Initial empty or evidence-rejected pools do not trigger refresh.

requirements.title: Knowledge and fictional content
requirements.text: Support care, geology, type comparisons and the playful stone personalities from the encyclopedia. Mark personality, preference and ritual material as fictional, both in indexed metadata and answers; preserve the source's introductory qualification. Do not imply that stones need feeding, watering, sunlight, medical treatment or possess healing powers. Distinguish a typical type property from an examined individual fact. Knowledge sources are reviewed encyclopedia passages and current catalog facts; when evidence is insufficient, say so. Unretrieved model memory may help phrase a response but is not evidence for a new factual claim.

requirements.title: Grounded answer presentation
requirements.text: Selection explanations cover every presented stone and its matched/unmatched wishes without adding or reordering IDs. Mixed queries combine selection with requested care topics; knowledge-only replies have no specimen links unless resolving a current reference. Keep answer body plain text, with separate catalog links and an optional Sources disclosure listing human-readable document/topic labels and version-backed source links. Never expose storage credentials, raw object keys, vector scores or checker internals. Fiction labels remain visible without requiring the disclosure to be opened.

requirements.title: Model limits and completion fallback
requirements.text: Use a 120-second turn deadline, reserve its last five seconds for final checks/persistence, and bound each model call to 50 seconds or remaining work time. Context is 8192 tokens including output; interpretation/evidence output cap is 512 and final answer cap 1024. Trim old whole pairs within the latest 10 pairs/20000-character context bound; never truncate the current input or required evidence silently. Permit at most 20 evidence/check calls, four generation calls and two query embeddings per turn, with at most one correction per malformed batch/answer. No hidden provider retries.

requirements.title: Safe fallback and model failures
requirements.text: If candidate selection and evidence are valid but final explanation fails, discard unchecked prose and use a deterministic selection template preserving checked order, counts, partial wishes and alternatives, provided identity/history/catalog/accounting controls and deadline remain valid. This cannot rescue failed interpretation, invalid IDs, unchecked evidence or uncertain storage. Knowledge-only generation failure is an error, not a fabricated answer. One new successful pair is persisted atomically; an unknown commit is reconciled. Invalid structured output after permitted correction is 502 CHAT_INVALID_MODEL_OUTPUT.

requirements.title: Shared model admission and accounting
requirements.text: All backend model calls, including embeddings, share one per-instance invocation slot initially, configurable with zero customer queue. Retain the permit until execution actually exits. Use a durable PostgreSQL ledger, UTC daily budget 100000 input/output tokens; isolated qualification defaults to 200000 and preserves existing usage. Reserve a qualified upper bound before each call and settle actual usage; unknown usage remains reserved against its admission day. Initially retain the documented conservative 8192 chat and 32768 embedding bounds. Busy chat returns 503 CHAT_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, Retry-After 1; exhausted budget is 429 CHAT_TOKEN_BUDGET_EXCEEDED until next UTC day. Background indexing waits without consuming failure attempts.

sections.title: 9 Reference knowledge and reliable indexing
sections.sources: Features 0017 through 0023 and their AsyncAPI contracts
sections.intro: PostgreSQL remains authoritative for stones. MinIO keeps original reference documents; pgvector stores replaceable search projections. Kafka/outbox processing may lag, so public answers always validate live catalog eligibility. Recovery is an operator workflow with visible end-to-end state.

requirements.title: Document import and source preservation
requirements.text: Operator-only import reads the configured stone-encyclopedia_en.md object in the private stone-encyclopedia bucket, stable key stone-encyclopedia-en; callers cannot select arbitrary paths or upload Markdown through this operation. Enable source object versioning and retain the exact imported version/hash for as long as its projection or a retained answer citation references it. Never read or index engineering-log, aliases, symlinks or copies. Maximum UTF-8 source is 1 MiB and 2000 fragments; invalid text, no useful content or an indivisible oversized block is 422. Deleting a projection never deletes the source.

requirements.title: Passage construction and profiles
requirements.text: Split along stone and topic headings, preserving meaningful paragraphs/list items and table context. Include document, type and topic in embedded text; target approximately 500 tokens with 50-token overlap only within a split topic. Preserve original headings and source spans, shared applicability, language, content kind FACTUAL or FICTIONAL and SHA-256 version. Exclude navigation-only Contents; retain qualifications needed to interpret facts and fictional rituals. Use qwen3-embedding:0.6b with finite nonzero 1024-dimensional vectors, a recorded model digest/template profile and compatible query instruction; reject incompatible profiles rather than returning empty matches.

requirements.title: Atomic document publication and replay
requirements.text: Keep synchronous import for this local release, with 30-second connection, 5-minute source read, 30-minute single background embedding and 2-hour overall import limits; overall remaining time wins. Prepare all fragments/vectors before an atomic publication replacing the prior projection. Serialize mutation per document, reject overlap with 409, fence stale workers and reconcile uncertain commits. Require UUID-v4 Idempotency-Key on import/delete; replay successful status/result for 72 hours without rereading a changed source, then reject used keys retained for 90 days. A definitive started failure requires a new key. New import returns 201, replacement 200; no partially published index is visible.

requirements.title: Card projection and immutable events
requirements.text: Embed only name, type, size and biography, one vector per stone; no ID, status, date, photos or invented biography in the text. New stone sourceVersion starts at 1; indexed-field changes increment it, while no-op, photo/status/date changes do not. Commit a full-snapshot update or ID/version deletion event with the business mutation in one transaction. Event contains eventId UUID, eventType, schemaVersion 1, occurredAt UTC and a nonempty payload of at most 256 KiB compact UTF-8 JSON. Reused eventId must match type, schema version and canonical payload hash; mismatch fails. Return business success after commit without waiting for Kafka or models.

requirements.title: Outbox publication
requirements.text: One dispatcher polls every two seconds, up to 20 committed events, without holding a database transaction during Kafka I/O. Route STONE_CARD_INDEX_UPDATED and STONE_CARD_INDEX_DELETED to stone-card-index-events keyed by string stoneId; one partition, replication factor 1 for the local stack. Use producer idempotence and acks=all, but promise at-least-once delivery only. Persist PENDING, PUBLISHED, DEAD_LETTER_PENDING, DEAD_LETTERED, attempts, next attempt, error and timestamps. Event-specific failures allow three total attempts at 0, 2 and 4 seconds; dependency outage does not consume them. Retry DLQ transfer until acknowledged, preserving the original envelope and failure stage.

requirements.title: Consumer and deletion safety
requirements.text: One stone-card-indexer consumer starts at earliest retained records for a new group and resumes committed offsets after restart. Compute embeddings outside a database transaction, then atomically publish vector/text/version or delete vector and save a tombstone. Recheck sourceVersion at commit; incoming versions no greater than the durable version are skipped without model calls. Acknowledge only after database commit or acknowledged DLQ transfer. Persist retry count across restart, block the source partition during retry and wait on database/model/Kafka/capacity/budget outages. Malformed events and unsupported versions go directly to DLQ with lossless original data.

requirements.title: Reindex jobs and concurrent writes
requirements.text: Operator POST starts one durable ALL or SELECTED reindex job, returning 202 with jobId; selected IDs are positive, deduplicated, maximum 1000, and unknown selections fail before job creation. ALL captures a maximum stone ID and uses keyset batches of 20; later-created stones use normal events and are not blocked. Read each current snapshot, increment sourceVersion and write its outbox event atomically. Skip deleted rows; continue past per-item failures and pause on database outage. Reconcile orphan vectors using durable deletion guards. Resume after restart without recreating completed items.

requirements.title: End to end recovery state
requirements.text: Jobs progress QUEUED → ENQUEUING → APPLYING → SUCCEEDED or COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS; PAUSED preserves the prior stage and reason during dependency outage. ENQUEUED is a progress milestone, not completion. Track each item's target version/event and consumer outcome. A target is satisfied by that version or a newer valid applied version/tombstone; a terminal DLQ is an item error. Expose counts selected, enqueued, applied, superseded, skipped and failed, timestamps and bounded per-item error pages. No cancel endpoint in this release. Explicit retry of failed items creates a linked new job, not deletion of original evidence.

requirements.title: Retention and recovery visibility
requirements.text: Retain Kafka indexing and DLQ records for seven days, configurable; retain pending/error outbox records until resolved and acknowledged successful rows for 30 days. Keep consumer version/tombstone guards indefinitely while IDs can appear in retained work; job history 90 days. Detect lag approaching retention (24-hour warning, 6-day critical) and expose a degraded-index indicator to the operator. If records have expired, mark affected processing as requiring reconciliation and run an explicitly started ALL reindex. Never present stale index health as a successful empty search. Provide operator DLQ inspection and retry through current-source reindexing, not blind replay of obsolete snapshots.

sections.title: 10 HTTP and security contracts
sections.sources: Features 0003, 0004, 0006 through 0012, 0016, 0017, 0023, 0028; new operations are specified below
sections.intro: The operation inventory below fixes business-level routes, payload obligations, statuses and authorization. Implementation generates the full OpenAPI JSON/YAML from controllers and shared DTOs, including failure responses. Breaking changes apply to the new checkout; no in-place production migration is authorized by this document.

requirements.title: Common HTTP behavior
requirements.text: Use JSON and application/problem+json RFC 9457 errors with type, title, status, safe detail, instance and a stable code; validation adds fieldErrors. Do not expose stack traces or secret configuration. 400 covers syntax/field validation, 401 missing staff authentication, 403 denied action or Origin/CSRF, 404 absent or deliberately concealed resource, 409 business/idempotency conflict, 412 stale ETag, 413 oversized upload, 415 unsupported image, 422 unindexable document, 428 missing If-Match, 429 quota, 502 invalid model output and 503 unavailable dependency. Retry-After is supplied only with known guidance. [E01]

requirements.title: Staff authentication and sessions
requirements.text: Provide staff sign in at /stone-shelter/staff/sign-in using locally provisioned usernames and passwords; no registration/reset mail flow. Store passwords with a vetted framework encoder, BCrypt cost 12, and enforce 12–72 UTF-8 bytes for new passwords without truncation. Bootstrap an OPERATOR through a local provisioning command reading a secret from standard input; no default password. Session cookie is opaque, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, host-only and Secure on HTTPS, with 30-minute inactivity and 8-hour absolute expiry. Rotate ID on login, invalidate on logout; throttle login at 5 failed attempts per account and 20 per IP per 15 minutes with Retry-After. Require CSRF token and allowed Origin for cookie-authenticated mutations.

requirements.title: Public boundaries and isolation
requirements.text: Public read APIs remain unauthenticated. Anonymous application sessions use a separate opaque cookie and shared rate storage; Chat cookies use Path=/api/v1/chat; application cookies use Path=/api/v1; staff cookies use Path=/api to cover both versioned staff routes and the protected encyclopedia import route. Session creation is rate limited. Use actual peer IP unless the request arrives through an explicitly trusted proxy which replaces incoming forwarded headers. Same-origin deployment is default; approved CORS origins are explicit, never wildcard with credentials. Local published service ports bind to loopback. Deploying outside the local machine requires HTTPS and explicit deployment qualification; it is not part of this release. Application-session authority lasts 72 hours after the latest new committed application, without refresh on replay; cookie loss never transfers another session's idempotency ownership.

requirements.title: Generated contracts and versioning
requirements.text: Generate /v3/api-docs and /v3/api-docs.yaml with equivalent constraints, success/error schemas, authentication, idempotency/precondition headers and SSE lifecycle; generated operations cover application routes and exclude Actuator internals. Maintain Kafka contracts in AsyncAPI before implementation; increasing event structure incompatibly requires a new schemaVersion and tested consumer behavior. Do not preserve historical unsafe compatibility merely because an early stub accepted it. Record removed input fields and added staff protection in release migration notes.

requirements.title: Response representations
requirements.text: A public photo contains id, position, addedAt, processingStatus and nullable url; id is a UUID, position is zero-based. Public stone contains id, name, stoneType, stoneSize, biography, adoptionStatus, admissionDate and photos. Chat success and completed payload contain text, stones and sources; each stone is {id,name}, each source is {id,label,url,contentKind}, with backend-created same-origin version-backed URLs. History is {conversationId,messages}; each message has role, turnId, text, stones, sources and nullable context. USER entries have empty arrays and captured context; ASSISTANT entries have null context. Arrays are never null. This intentionally extends the historical two-field answer contract.

requirements.title: Search and operational request representations
requirements.text: Catalog search accepts stoneTypes[], stoneSizes[], optional adoptionStatus, admissionDateFrom/To UTC instants, page, size and one sort object {field,direction}; To is exclusive. Supported sort fields are admissionDate, name and stoneSize. Omitted sort uses Newest first; the UI sends explicit page/size. Legacy singular type/size filters are removed in the new baseline. Staff PUT uses wire names stoneType and stoneSize. Photo append and reindex start use the 72-hour replay/90-day marker policy of R029; a reindex retry returns the original job, not a second job. Jobs expose errors as {items,page,size,totalElements}, page size default 20, maximum 100.

requirements.title: Read expiry and session mutation details
requirements.text: Public stone status is effective status at the read transaction timestamp: an unexpired PENDING hold means RESERVED, a completed application means ADOPTED, otherwise AVAILABLE. Search/count and detail use this same rule. Read operations do not mutate expiry state; write guards and the expiry worker reconcile due rows transactionally before creating new holds. Anonymous application creation obtains or validates an application session under the IP gate; browser POST requires an allowed Origin. The response key replay namespace follows that server session, never an actor ID supplied in JSON. Public source excerpts include only reviewed published text, not arbitrary bucket reads.

sections.title: 11 Quality attributes and implementation constraints
sections.sources: Constitution, stack ADRs, feature plans and cited primary guidance
sections.intro: The requirements below are measurable release obligations. Numerical service targets are product choices for the local qualification fixture, not universal benchmarks or claims that the present application achieves them. Dependency pins copied from project decisions require a fresh installation and compatibility check in the new checkout.

requirements.title: Accessibility and responsive layout
requirements.text: Target WCAG 2.2 AA across the stated workflows: meaningful labels/headings, keyboard access, visible and unobscured focus, error association, sufficient contrast and text scaling. Support 320 CSS px without horizontal page scroll, 200% text zoom and reduced motion. Interactive targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS px, preferably 44 for primary touch actions. Test with keyboard and a screen reader as well as automation. Modal behavior follows the WAI-ARIA dialog pattern. Replace the Russian text embedded in the placeholder with English accessible content. [E02, E05]

requirements.title: Operational targets
requirements.text: On a declared local reference machine, with warm services, 1000 stones and ten concurrent non-model clients, catalog/detail server p95 is at most 500 ms and non-photo writes p95 at most 1 second, excluding network rendering and background models. Upload has a 60-second request bound and visible progress. Under idle model capacity, no backlog and sufficient quota, 95% of new or changed cards become searchable within 5 minutes; slower cases are visible as delayed, not falsely complete. Record machine, fixture and sample size (at least 100 reads, 30 writes, 20 index events); failure blocks the applicable gate. AI uses bounded deadlines and separate quality evaluation, not an invented instant-response promise.

requirements.title: Architecture and persistence
requirements.text: Use Spring MVC controllers for routes/binding/validation/statuses; services own business orchestration and transactions; repositories own queries, Criteria and ordering; mappers construct responses. Controllers never expose entities. Shared DTOs live outside controllers; services do not depend on web handlers or JPA query APIs. Follow the existing mapper naming/direction rules and record/class convention for this initial checkout; enforce only syntactically reliable parts mechanically. Liquibase owns schema; never rewrite an applied migration. Use PostgreSQL/Testcontainers rather than H2 for persistence/concurrency verification.

requirements.title: Dependency and configuration discipline
requirements.text: Start from the documented stack pins: JDK 23.0.2, Spring Boot 4.1.1, Spring AI 2.0.1, PostgreSQL 18.6, pgvector 0.8.6, Redis 8.2.10, Kafka 4.2.2, Ollama 0.40.3, Node 24.21.0/npm 11.19.0, React 19.3.0, TypeScript 6.0.3, Vite 8.3.2 and Router 8.4.0. These are source-recorded selections, not independently certified installed versions. W01 verifies availability, exact digests and compatibility; an unavailable/incompatible pin blocks implementation until an explicit version ADR amendment, with no silent substitution. Pin all direct tools/dependencies, use lockfiles, no latest, no secret values in documentation or reports.

requirements.title: Environment readiness throughout tests
requirements.text: Every authorized implementation/test batch begins with a readiness ticket listing every covered task and its prerequisites. Check command-scoped JAVA_HOME/Maven, Node/npm, required models/digests, browser installation, effective endpoints and installed source versions. Probe from the execution context used by the tests: API HTTP/database connectivity, frontend route, MinIO, Redis operations, Kafka metadata and model inventory as applicable. Distinguish READY, BLOCKED and NOT_REQUIRED; a running container alone is insufficient. Do not use business imports or application tests as preflight. Provision only approved isolated resources; never mutate the original checkout.

requirements.title: Readiness guard and evidence freshness
requirements.text: The integration-test runner owns bounded readiness before start, every 15 seconds while tests run, and after completion; it records failures without running business operations as probes. Required capability loss terminates dependent execution safely and marks the run BLOCKED_ENVIRONMENT, retaining any already-observed product failure. Reports bind checkout commit plus dirty-tree content digest, configuration/schema/model identities, task IDs, endpoints, timestamps and command exit codes. Any relevant content/config change invalidates prior evidence. Missing, stale, skipped or synthetic evidence cannot pass a gate; a docs-only task does not require an application stack.

requirements.title: Deterministic static gate before review
requirements.text: Before developer handoff, a mandatory wrapper runs pinned Java Checkstyle, PMD with standard and project-specific rules, React/TypeScript ESLint, type checking and relevant architecture checks. Java uses a Google-style configuration bundled with the pinned Checkstyle release with documented project exceptions; React uses ESLint recommended, typescript-eslint, hooks and accessibility rules because Java Checkstyle does not analyze React. PMD checks feasible DTO/package/layer/mapping constraints; semantic business policies remain review or architecture tests, never a false PMD guarantee. Nonzero exit, missing report or unapproved suppression prevents reviewer handoff. SonarQube analysis and its quality gate are additional required release evidence, never substitutes for the local tools. [E07–E10]

requirements.title: Quality gate rules
requirements.text: Require zero new Checkstyle/PMD/ESLint/type errors, zero blocker/critical/high unresolved security findings, passing required architecture/contract/unit/integration/browser scenarios, and no new critical/serious automated accessibility violations. SonarQube new-code coverage is at least 80% and duplication at most 3%, with new reliability/security issues resolved and security hotspots reviewed. Maintain a meaningful focused test selector per ticket; full regression runs only at an explicitly authorized release gate. Record exact configured thresholds and tool versions in the checkout, not only prose; no silent local/CI differences.

requirements.title: Agent handoff and completion
requirements.text: Development swarm receives spec/scenarios, scope allowlist and fresh readiness. Planner returns task/dependency mapping; developer returns patch and static-gate evidence; independent reviewer returns APPROVED or actionable findings. Test swarm receives the reviewed content digest and scenarios; test engineer returns focused automated results, and test reviewer independently checks coverage, negative/concurrent cases and evidence. Only TEST_REVIEW_APPROVED opens manual browser swarm: scenario planner supplies charters, Playwright browser agent performs real app workflows, independent acceptance reviewer checks screenshots/traces/results. The deterministic final gate sets DONE only when all required evidence and all three review stages approve the same content. Any relevant change invalidates downstream approvals.

requirements.title: Manual browser evidence
requirements.text: Manual swarm means agent-guided exploratory and scripted inspection in a real browser, not a claim that a human tested it. Exercise actual API-backed create, details, filters, reservation, staff resolution, photo failures, streaming recovery and reload, plus developer-mock mode parity. Capture scenario ID, viewport, initial data IDs, actions, expected/observed result and trace/screenshot. Use synthetic contacts and an isolated fixture; never treat a static screenshot, mocked API run or prior source test result as live application acceptance. Do not connect a ticket board in this release.

requirements.title: AI qualification gate
requirements.text: Retain the source fixed-set structure of 20 scenarios and 28 turns, nine semantic and twelve ordinary-answer scenarios, plus controlled race/failure checks; revise only changed oracles through a versioned fixture change before evaluation. Require all hard invariants, at least 8/9 semantic and 10/12 ordinary-answer scenarios. Grounding, constraints, references, fiction labels and truthful source attribution are independent oracles. A valid template is functional fallback, not successful ordinary generation. Record original attempts and reviewer identity; interruptions remain incomplete and denominators never shrink. Existing source results report semantic 2/9, ordinary answer 0/12 and incomplete controls, so they do not pass this release. Section 16 fixes the SS-QUAL-1.0 data and amended query oracles; its explanation requests distinguish generated-answer scoring from ordinary deterministic exact search.

requirements.title: Observability and data protection
requirements.text: Record request/correlation IDs, stable error codes, queue lag, model-admission outcomes and stage durations without raw applicant contacts, passwords, cookies, tokens or full prompts. Store operational logs for seven days; audit privileged actions for 90 days without private free text. Expose capability-specific status and last-check time to operators; public readiness contains no sensitive inventory. Backup PostgreSQL and permanent/source object storage before destructive migration; demonstrate restore in an isolated environment. Redis conversation loss is a documented local limitation and cannot authorize ownership transfer.

decisions.subject: A single current baseline
decisions.previous: Early features were mocks and controller stubs; later features replaced them.
decisions.target: Use real API-backed catalog and grounded chat; preserve explicitly selected developer mock mode.
decisions.reason: Historical milestones cannot all be simultaneous product requirements.

decisions.subject: Staff permissions
decisions.previous: Creation, uploads and document import were open or had no ownership contract.
decisions.target: Authenticate volunteers/operators and bind drafts to their staff owner.
decisions.reason: Prevent unauthorized mutation and draft theft while leaving discovery and applications public; E03 and E04.

decisions.subject: Server controlled fields
decisions.previous: Early create/update accepted status and admission date.
decisions.target: Create assigns AVAILABLE and UTC time; ordinary updates cannot write either.
decisions.reason: One lifecycle owner avoids contradictory status and history.

decisions.subject: Complete adoption lifecycle
decisions.previous: One reservation ever per stone, with no expiry or staff resolution.
decisions.target: One active hold, 72-hour expiry, one extension, complete/cancel/reject actions and a staff queue.
decisions.reason: Applications can be resolved and abandoned holds do not permanently remove inventory.

decisions.subject: Bounded personal information
decisions.previous: Applicant fields had no business maximum or retention.
decisions.target: Name 120/contact 1000; purge PII 30 days after terminal status and keep minimal audit 90 days.
decisions.reason: Data minimization and predictable validation; these are product limits, not jurisdiction-specific legal claims.

decisions.subject: Safe write retry
decisions.previous: Several create flows had only a disabled button and manual retries.
decisions.target: Server idempotency with 72-hour saved results and 90-day used-key markers plus lost-acknowledgement reconciliation.
decisions.reason: An HTTP timeout does not prove that the transaction failed.

decisions.subject: A usable photo form
decisions.previous: Screenshot 4 and feature 0009 allocate 16 empty photo slots.
decisions.target: Progressive responsive previews, count/limit guidance, add/remove/reorder and keyboard controls.
decisions.reason: Preserves optional 16-photo capacity while reducing empty scrolling and improving mobile use.

decisions.subject: Consistent gallery limits
decisions.previous: Initial uploads capped at 16 but append was uncapped; gallery edits omitted.
decisions.target: Apply 16 across all paths and support removal/reordering under concurrency protection.
decisions.reason: One invariant across UI/API prevents growth and inconsistent cover behavior.

decisions.subject: Photo repair
decisions.previous: A failed permanent copy could keep its claimed source forever with no repair route.
decisions.target: Durable bounded retries, visible processing states and staff repair/remove actions.
decisions.reason: A successful stone creation must have a path to recover its photos.

decisions.subject: Managed images only
decisions.previous: Legacy arbitrary photo URLs were preserved.
decisions.target: New writes accept managed photos only; legacy conversion is an explicit migration.
decisions.reason: Avoid uncontrolled tracking/content URLs and maintain a predictable image lifecycle.

decisions.subject: Fiction remains fiction
decisions.previous: The original encyclopedia explains fictional personalities, but indexing explicitly removed that qualification.
decisions.target: Preserve factual/fictional metadata and disclose fictional rituals in answers.
decisions.reason: The source itself distinguishes reality and play; removing that distinction makes care guidance misleading.

decisions.subject: Visible evidence
decisions.previous: Feature 0026 prohibited all visible source attribution.
decisions.target: Optional human-readable Sources disclosure with version-backed excerpts.
decisions.reason: Visitors can inspect the basis of a factual answer without seeing internal scores or keys.

decisions.subject: Explicit broad searches
decisions.previous: Availability-only requests were forced into at least two clarification questions.
decisions.target: Honor explicit Show all available requests with five newest results; clarify genuinely vague intent.
decisions.reason: The visitor has already specified a valid catalog action; unnecessary questioning adds friction.

decisions.subject: Useful no match outcomes
decisions.previous: Zero selections required absence-only text.
decisions.target: Report no match and offer an optional refinement suggestion without applying it automatically.
decisions.reason: The user keeps control of constraints while receiving a recovery path.

decisions.subject: Read history during model outage
decisions.previous: Global chat failure closed sends, history and committed replay when Ollama failed.
decisions.target: Gate each capability on its own prerequisites; healthy owned history/replay remains readable.
decisions.reason: Completed data recovery should not require an unrelated model service.

decisions.subject: Finish the interrupted answer policy
decisions.previous: Partial-answer retention was explicitly provisional.
decisions.target: Keep received text as Incomplete without links, reconcile manually and never auto-resend.
decisions.reason: Makes transport uncertainty understandable without misrepresenting saved completion.

decisions.subject: Conversation controls
decisions.previous: New/clear conversation controls were excluded.
decisions.target: Add new conversation and authorized clear with active-turn conflict protection.
decisions.reason: Visitors need a bounded way to reset context and remove retained chat data.

decisions.subject: Recoverable source provenance
decisions.previous: Only the currently overwritten MinIO source was retained.
decisions.target: Keep imported object versions while referenced by projections or retained citations.
decisions.reason: A citation hash must resolve to the content that actually supported the answer.

decisions.subject: Immutable event identity
decisions.previous: A matching eventId ignored changed payload content.
decisions.target: Compare canonical payload hash as well as type/version and fail on mismatch.
decisions.reason: Detect accidental identity reuse instead of concealing a lost business event.

decisions.subject: Reindex without blocking creation
decisions.previous: ALL reindex blocked new stone creation until enqueue finished.
decisions.target: Snapshot an ID high-water mark; ordinary events cover subsequent creates.
decisions.reason: Maintains availability while preserving a finite reproducible job target.

decisions.subject: Actual reindex completion
decisions.previous: ENQUEUED was the only terminal success and end-to-end tracking was deferred.
decisions.target: Track consumer application/supersession and terminate SUCCEEDED or COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS.
decisions.reason: Operators need to distinguish durable intent from searchable results.

decisions.subject: Bounded retention and observability
decisions.previous: Kafka retention was 24 hours; outbox/jobs were indefinite and metrics deferred.
decisions.target: Kafka 7 days, successful outbox 30 days, jobs 90 days, unresolved work retained and lag alerts.
decisions.reason: Provides a practical recovery window and avoids silent unlimited storage growth.

decisions.subject: Real browser completion evidence
decisions.previous: Some feature acceptance allowed missing browser checks or omitted mock submissions.
decisions.target: Require real API browser workflows and independently reviewed evidence before DONE.
decisions.reason: Unit/lint success does not establish that the screenshot workflows are usable.

decisions.subject: Performance and AI release evidence
decisions.previous: Performance checks were excluded and broad AI qualification remains failed/incomplete.
decisions.target: Add bounded local service targets and make the fixed-set AI gate mandatory, preserving original results.
decisions.reason: A ready specification must define observable release criteria rather than inherit historical waivers.

decisions.subject: Small educational deployment
decisions.previous: Multiple backend processes, external providers and analytics were deferred.
decisions.target: Keep one active backend, local models, no analytics feature or ticket-board connector.
decisions.reason: Reliability improvements address current workflows without introducing an unrelated platform.

decisions.subject: API clarity and error documentation
decisions.previous: Early OpenAPI documented success only and several DTOs omitted new state.
decisions.target: Generate full success/error/security contracts and explicitly extend photo/chat/job representations.
decisions.reason: Consumers need one authoritative generated contract for the chosen behavior; E01.

Persistent stone model, generated API, fixtures, catalog/detail UI, filters, navigation and accessibility.
Draft ownership, atomic creation, transfer/cleanup, staff edit/gallery, write replay and source migration notes.
Visitor application, concurrent hold, staff queue/transitions, expiry and privacy lifecycle.
Versioned encyclopedia import, profile qualification, outbox/consumer/DLQ, reindex and operational status.
Owned memory, rate/concurrency/budget controls, exact/semantic/knowledge behavior and source disclosures.
SSE protocol, UI parsing, interruption/reload/cookie reconciliation, responsive browser verification.
Fixed-set AI evidence, focused regression aggregation, performance/accessibility/restore checks and final gate.

acceptance.title: Scope and permissions
acceptance.given: A clean implementation checkout and the baseline
acceptance.when: Review the release scope and call each privileged route as visitor, volunteer and operator
acceptance.then: Only the role matrix grants access; no deferred capability is presented as delivered; generated contracts implement this baseline
acceptance.method: Document review and API authorization matrix

acceptance.title: Domain boundaries
acceptance.given: Records with every enum and Unicode boundary fixture
acceptance.when: Create with valid values, at limit and one beyond; submit client status/date; read publicly
acceptance.then: Valid records persist with server AVAILABLE/UTC; invalid fields reject with 400; code-point counts match UI; no private fields appear
acceptance.method: DTO validation, API and mapper tests

acceptance.title: Stale updates and deletion
acceptance.given: Two staff clients share an ETag and a separate stone has an active hold
acceptance.when: Save from both clients; omit If-Match; attempt deletion of held and free stones
acceptance.then: First save succeeds, stale requests return 412, missing preconditions return 428, active hold returns 409; valid delete hides the stone and preserves tombstone/cleanup intent
acceptance.method: PostgreSQL concurrent integration test

acceptance.title: Routes and return state
acceptance.given: A filtered paginated catalog is scrolled down
acceptance.when: Open a detail, use Back/Forward and Back to catalog; refresh canonical/legacy/unknown routes
acceptance.then: Session catalog state restores; direct/reload defaults apply; canonical redirects replace history; missing record and unknown route are distinct
acceptance.method: Playwright API-mode navigation

acceptance.title: Filtering and counts
acceptance.given: A fixed catalog contains available/reserved/adopted stones across types, sizes and UTC day boundaries
acceptance.when: Apply two sizes, two types and From/To; sort all six ways; paginate; request non-AVAILABLE status
